quotes.text: **Dispute activity** represents the percentage of disputes on successful payments by *dispute* date.
**Dispute rate** represents the percentage of disputes on successful payments by *charge* date.
In some cases, our AI models can predict if your account might be in danger of excessive dispute activity at a point in the future. If that happens, we’ll alert you

Because cardholders can dispute a charge up to 120 days after a payment was made ([and sometimes even later](https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/how-disputes-work.md#timing)), the dispute rate might change for dates more recent than 120 days old.
Visa in particular counts these fraud warnings toward identification in their [VAMP monitoring program](https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/monitoring-programs.md#VAMP).

findings: Both captures define dispute activity by dispute date and dispute rate by original charge date, each over successful payments, with the same 1,000-payment/10-dispute/3-same-week example yielding 1% activity and 0.3% rate (old 8-18; new 9-19). The current source 15-24 and wiki/concepts/disputes.md 142-149 preserve this distinction.

Both captures say network monitoring programs use dispute activity, while charge-date dispute rate helps find problematic payments and fraud patterns (old 20-29; new 21-30). Activity above 0.75% is called excessive as an industry standard, but sudden spikes or trends can trigger monitoring earlier, and prolonged network-threshold excess may cause fines (old 22, 34-36; new 23, 35-37). No account-specific program threshold or actual fine is established.

Both warn that charge-date dispute rate can change for dates under 120 days old and that cardholders sometimes dispute even later (old line 29; new line 30). Current source line 35 and disputes concept line 149 compress this to '<120 days', which can mislead a query about whether rates become final after day 120. Correct both to state the ordinary window and explicit later-dispute exception; the capture gives no fixed finality date.

Both say only in some cases can Stripe's AI models predict future excessive activity, and only if that happens will Stripe alert the account; individual future disputes and the predicted rate remain uncertain (old lines 38-43; new lines 39-44). Current source line 39 unconditionally says the models predict and alert proactively. Correct that existing source claim now, rather than merely noting a caveat for future reuse. No account-specific alert is established.

Both identify EFWs as issuer-generated suspected-fraud messages on Visa, Mastercard and JCB; EFWs may enable refund before a fraud dispute and matter as network fraud metrics, with Visa using them for VAMP identification (old 45-49; new 46-50). No automatic conversion into a dispute or guaranteed avoidance from refund follows.

The 74-line diff changes italics, heading spaces, three chart image references, 'Radar for Fraud Teams' to 'Radar' at the same Dashboard route, and one See also link (diff 3-74). unresolved_questions: The snapshots do not verify present network-monitoring program numeric thresholds, account placement, fee assessment, exact Radar access or a live dispute-rate calculation.
The captured prediction text does not establish a particular payment will be disputed or that an alert is always delivered.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/measuring, both captures distinguish dispute-date activity, used for network monitoring, from charge-date dispute rate, used for fraud and sale pattern analysis (new lines 9-30; old lines 8-29). The example remains ten disputes received among one thousand weekly payments, three on that week's charges, yielding 1% activity and 0.3% rate (new lines 15-19; old lines 14-18). [[source-stripe-disputes-measuring]] records that distinction, but its prediction and 120-day wording need corrective qualification even though the capture changed no metric formula.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/measuring, [[source-stripe-disputes-measuring]] requires a corrective source update despite presentational/navigation differences: source line 39 should say Stripe predicts excessive activity only in some cases and alerts if it does, without certainty for individual payments or the rate (old lines 40-43; new lines 41-44). Source line 35 and disputes concept line 149 must allow disputes after 120 days (old line 29; new line 30). Keep >0.75% as an industry warning, distinct from network-set prolonged thresholds and possible earlier placement after spikes (old lines 22, 34-36; new lines 23, 35-37).
